FOLDER_Finding: Relationship organization is represented in the patient-level EHR Directory through FOLDER hierarchy and membership references.
LINK_Finding: Relationships are represented explicitly as RM LINK structures owned by the relevant LOCATABLE, with direction and target determined by the implementation design.
CLUSTER_Finding: Relationship information is represented as archetyped CLUSTER content embedded in the relevant modeled clinical or contextual structure.
Evidence_Boundary: Identifies where each evaluated design represents relationship information. It does not establish production suitability or comparative performance.

FOLDER_Finding: Relationship organization is governed primarily through directory structure and conventions, while FOLDER can additionally carry archetyped metadata through details.
FOLDER_Evidence_Type: Specification; Design artifact; Comparative architectural inference
LINK_Finding: The RM provides the LINK mechanism and relationship meaning. Consistent implementation additionally depends on shared conventions for relationship type, direction, target, and granularity.
LINK_Evidence_Type: Specification; Design artifact; Comparative architectural inference
CLUSTER_Finding: Relationship elements, structural cardinalities, role values, and other value constraints can be governed explicitly through archetypes and templates. In the ENTRY-level relationship archetype, each repeated Episode reference pairs one Link with one Role constrained to Primary or Associated. The additional model-level invariant requiring exactly one Primary Episode association per clinical ENTRY is not independently enforced by the archetype. These constraints do not by themselves validate the existence of referenced targets.
Evidence_Boundary: Supports comparison of governance location in the evaluated designs. 'Strongest in-template semantic governance' is a comparative finding within this study, not a universal superiority claim. Archetype/template constraints describe permitted structures and values, not automatic enforcement of all cross-reference or clinical invariants. In T5, the RI-02 negative test recorded acceptance of a dangling relationship reference (HTTP 201); referential integrity was not enforced in that scenario.

Architectural_Concern: Relationship granularity in the evaluated design
FOLDER_Finding: The evaluated hierarchy organizes references at patient-level Directory and nested FOLDER level, including Care Encounter-, Episode-, and Clinical Section-oriented groupings.
LINK_Finding: The evaluated design uses COMPOSITION-level relationships for Care Encounter association and ENTRY-level relationships for Episode association. Complementary technical PoC variants examined context-to-clinical LINK direction (T2) and clinical-to-context LINK direction (T3); these are implementation variants, not changes to the original design-level comparison.
CLUSTER_Finding: The evaluated design uses relationship CLUSTERs at ENTRY, Care Encounter COMPOSITION, and Episode-of-Care COMPOSITION contexts. The technical PoC additionally examined context-to-clinical relationship CLUSTERs (T4) and ENTRY-level clinical-to-context relationship CLUSTERs (T5).
Evidence_Boundary: Describes the granularity selected for this study. It does not imply that these are the only RM-conformant granularities possible. The T2–T5 tests document selected technical directions and persistence/retrieval scenarios in EHRbase, not an exhaustive evaluation of all permissible relationship granularities.

FOLDER_Finding: Existing clinical objects can be referenced from multiple Episode-oriented FOLDER nodes without duplicating the referenced clinical content.
LINK_Finding: A clinical ENTRY can carry multiple LINKs to Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs, with implementation conventions distinguishing a primary Episode from additional associated Episodes.
CLUSTER_Finding: The ENTRY-level relationship CLUSTER permits one or more Episode references. Each repeated Episode reference contains exactly one Link to an Episode-of-Care COMPOSITION and exactly one Role constrained to Primary or Associated. The additional model-level invariant requiring exactly one Primary Episode association per clinical ENTRY requires additional validation.
Evidence_Boundary: Demonstrates structural representability and explicit Link/Role pairing for multiple Episode associations. It does not demonstrate archetype-level enforcement of exactly one Primary Episode association, clinical correctness of every association, or an automated association workflow. A complete SOAP progress note is one clinical documentation unit even when represented by four technical OBSERVATION.progress_note.v1 ENTRYs under SECTION.soap.v0. The intended Episode-of-Care assignment must remain consistent across these technical components; the PoC does not establish automated enforcement of that clinical-unit invariant.

FOLDER_Finding: FOLDER provides an explicit patient-level hierarchical index over existing EHR objects and can expose Care Encounter-, Episode-, and Clinical Section-oriented navigation structures.
LINK_Finding: LINK provides explicit object relationships but does not itself constitute a patient-wide hierarchical navigation structure. Such navigation must be assembled from relationships and application/query logic.
CLUSTER_Finding: CLUSTER exposes governed relationship metadata but does not itself constitute a patient-wide navigation hierarchy. Navigation is derived through query/application projections.
Evidence_Boundary: Compares structural support for navigation, not user-interface usability or navigation performance.

FOLDER_Finding: Retrieval follows Directory traversal and resolution of referenced EHR objects.
LINK_Finding: Retrieval follows relationship traversal and target resolution where required information resides in the LINK target.
LINK_Evidence_Type: Specification; Design artifact; Comparative architectural inference
CLUSTER_Finding: Locally represented relationship metadata can participate in AQL filtering and projection through stable archetyped paths. Referenced target information still requires target resolution.
Evidence_Boundary: Concerns logical query structure only. No comparative benchmark of latency, throughput, execution plans, or production-scale workloads was performed. The EHRbase PoC documented selected Directory operations and references (T0–T1), LINK persistence and selected retrieval (T2–T3), and CLUSTER persistence plus AQL-based extraction of relationship metadata (T4–T5). These observations do not demonstrate complete automated clinical-view assembly or universal target dereferencing. Illustrative AQL examples under 06-retrieval-examples are distinct from executed queries archived under 08-technical-proof-of-concept.

FOLDER_Finding: Directory organization is versioned independently from referenced clinical content. The complete FOLDER hierarchy is managed as a VERSIONED_FOLDER rather than as independently versioned FOLDER subtrees.
LINK_Finding: LINK is part of its owning LOCATABLE. Relationship changes therefore follow the version lifecycle of the containing version-controlled object, typically the owning COMPOSITION in the evaluated design.
CLUSTER_Finding: Relationship CLUSTERs are persisted within their containing COMPOSITION. Relationship changes therefore follow the version lifecycle of that COMPOSITION.
CLUSTER_Evidence_Type: Specification; Design artifact; Comparative architectural inference
Evidence_Boundary: Describes lifecycle coupling implied by the RM and evaluated design. Concurrency and large-scale update behavior were not empirically tested.

FOLDER_Finding: Primary responsibility lies in Directory provisioning, hierarchy maintenance, traversal, and reference management.
LINK_Finding: Primary responsibility lies in application/integration logic for relationship creation, direction conventions, traversal, and target resolution.
CLUSTER_Finding: Primary responsibility lies in archetype/template modeling and governance, with applications populating and querying the constrained relationship structures.
Evidence_Boundary: Architectural allocation of responsibility is inferred from the evaluated designs and RM mechanisms. Development effort was not measured.

FOLDER_Finding: Consistent cross-system use depends on shared interpretation of Directory structures and referenced identifiers.
LINK_Finding: Consistent cross-system use depends on consistent interpretation of LINK relationship meanings, shared conventions for type and direction, and target-resolution mechanisms.
CLUSTER_Finding: Shared archetypes and templates can communicate relationship structure and constraints, while terminology, identifiers, and reference-resolution conventions remain additional dependencies.
Evidence_Boundary: Identifies prerequisites for cross-CDR interpretation. The study did not empirically demonstrate multi-vendor or cross-repository interoperability.

Architectural_Concern: Principal strength in the evaluated design
FOLDER_Finding: Provides explicit patient-level hierarchical organization and navigation over existing EHR content.
LINK_Finding: Provides an explicit native RM mechanism for object-to-object relationships without requiring a separate relationship archetype.
CLUSTER_Finding: Provides explicit archetype/template-level governance of relationship structure, structural cardinalities, constrained role values, and queryable paths.
Evidence_Boundary: Strengths are comparative architectural findings within the evaluated design and requirements, not universal rankings.

Architectural_Concern: Principal trade-off in the evaluated design
FOLDER_Finding: Requires Directory provisioning and maintenance, hierarchy-level update lifecycle management, and additional traversal/reference resolution.
LINK_Finding: Requires shared conventions and application/integration logic for relationship direction, type, target selection, traversal, and resolution.
CLUSTER_Finding: Requires dedicated modeling and template governance and couples relationship changes to the version lifecycle of the containing COMPOSITION.
Evidence_Boundary: Trade-offs describe architectural responsibilities and lifecycle implications. They are not measured cost, complexity, or performance outcomes.
